tailMarker.anomalyNote: The earliest tail-class ingredient is a COLOURANT at rank 7 — the only cohort product where the marker is neither a fragrance nor a preservative, and the only one where Parfum is the FINAL entry (rank 30). §3.1's literal anomaly conditions are not met (rank 7 > 3, and Cetearyl Alcohol @2 and Behentrimonium Chloride @4 precede it), so the marker is technically resolved. But a colourant pair at ranks 7–8 in a list whose fragrance sits at 30 is not a plausible ~1% proxy: cosmetic colourants are typically used far below 1%, and this ordering is more consistent with a house listing convention or a retailer transcription artefact than with descending weight. I therefore fire `tail_marker_anomaly` by reviewer judgment and cap every affected field at moderate confidence, while still applying the marker as written. See AP-11-COLOURANT.  ||  TAIL MARKER RE-DERIVED UNDER v0.2 (R8 colourant precedence + R2 plausibility). v0.1 set tail_index = 7 on CI 17200/RED 33. Under Standard §3.1 and lexicon §0.2 as patched by R8, a colourant may no longer define the marker. Recomputing on the marker-eligible classes, the earliest is HYDROXYCITRONELLAL @12, a declared fragrance allergen named in §3.1's list. tail_index is therefore 12, not 7, and the credited segment grows from six entries to eleven, newly admitting CI 17200 @7 and CI 19140 @8 (recorded as E1 formula facts with zero care credit, exactly as Titanium Dioxide and Mica are - lexicon family 10), COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9, SODIUM CHLORIDE @10 (family 10, zero credit) and HYDROXYPROPYL GUAR @11 (non-ionic thickener, zero care credit; also the tail_index - 1 species). PLAUSIBILITY ASSESSMENT (R2, §3.1.1): PLAUSIBLE - CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2, BEHENTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @4, AMODIMETHICONE @6 and COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9 all outrank @12, and the product is a conventional O/W emulsion with AQUA/WATER @1. This closes v0.1's AP-11-COLOURANT, which fired `tail_marker_anomaly` by reviewer judgment: the anomaly is now resolved by rule rather than by judgment, and that trigger no longer fires. PARFUM/FRAGRANCE remains the final entry @30 - the house-convention pattern lexicon §0.2 warns about - and the allergen fallback is exactly what §0.2's marker-failure fallback prescribes.  ||  RE-DERIVED UNDER v0.3 (E2, §3.1.1 third limb, 2026-09-14): tail_marker = UNRESOLVED, plausible = false. R8's colourant demotion STANDS and is not reopened: a colourant may not set the marker, so recomputing on the marker-eligible classes still lands on HYDROXYCITRONELLAL @12 rather than on CI 17200 @7. E2 then tests whether the species recomputation lands on can be believed, and here it cannot. HYDROXYCITRONELLAL is a DECLARED FRAGRANCE ALLERGEN — a constituent OF the fragrance compound — and PARFUM/FRAGRANCE itself is the FINAL entry at rank 30. An allergen is by construction present in smaller quantity than the compound that carries it, so an allergen eighteen ranks ABOVE its own Parfum is not a descending-weight ordering; it is a house listing convention (the pattern lexicon §0.2 warns about) or a retailer transcription artefact. Taking it as the ~1 % proxy would put the fragrance compound and everything between rank 12 and rank 30 into the sub-1 % tail on the strength of one of its own trace constituents. Limbs 1 and 2 do not fire (every architecture-establishing species outranks @12; conventional O/W emulsion with AQUA/WATER @1); the third limb does. CONSEQUENCES under §3.1.1: the marker may not disqualify and may not qualify, confidence on every affected field is capped at `moderate`, `tail_marker_unresolved` fires, and nothing auto-decides in either direction. Concretely, clause 2 governs this record: COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9 was credited as above-tail architecture SOLELY because it outranks @12, so it may not be credited, and the v0.2 cascade it drove (weight moderate→high, focus shine→smoothing, thickness losing `fine`) is reverted to the conservative v0.1 reading. The competing reading — marker at PARFUM @30, everything credited — is recorded on each affected field and adjudicated in AP-11-MARKERUNRESOLVED. This does NOT revert to the colourant: E2 is a plausibility rule about whether a recomputed marker can be believed, not a fallback to a class R8 demoted.

primaryFocus.derivation: Step 1 baseline exclusion applied. Step 2: one M1 base observation plus one M3 optical observation. Step 3: `repair` blocked (no R5 at any rank, no bond token; R6a can never set repair); `curl_support` blocked (single cationic in the head, no established above-tail polymer); `color_care` blocked (the CI entries are the product's own dye load, and colour-DEPOSITING masks are excluded at G0 in any case); `lightness` blocked (weight_potential is `moderate`, not `low`). Step 4 `moisture` blocked at §9.5.3 criterion 1 (PROPYLENE GLYCOL @5 is the only humectant-class species with a secure position, against a required three). Step 5 `shine`: criterion 1 holds — the optical architecture is present and no R4b heavy lipid is established above the tail; criterion 2 holds — the amino silicone is a distinct addition to an unusually thin base, not the base's own film; criterion 3 holds on exact-product positioning, used as corroboration only. Selected.
thresholdReasoning: Criterion 1 CLEARS: an alignment-oriented R2 silicone above the tail with a comparatively low lipid load and no R4b heavy lipid established above the tail. The condition is met because §3.1.1 clause 2 withholds the coconut oil's above-tail credit — not because the species is absent. That distinction is stated plainly because it is the whole of the difference from v0.2.

Criterion 2 CLEARS: the optical route is not merely a smoothing film already counted. No smoothing focus was awarded, and the architecture is not the ordinary M1 deposition — a thin base with one alignment-oriented amino silicone is the shape §9.5.4 describes as distinguishing a gloss product from a rich nourishing mask.

Criterion 3 CLEARS on claim corroboration — the one legitimately claim-gated leg in this record. Gloss, Glaze, Laminierung and Glanz positioning are all present in the exact-product name and claims. Corroboration only: it could not have created the route, and criteria 1 and 2 were established blind.

THE COMPETING READING, RECORDED IN FULL (§3.1.1 clause 5): if the marker resolved at PARFUM @30, COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9 would be an established R4b heavy lipid above the tail, criterion 1's lipid condition would fail, §9.5.1's hard rule would forbid the gloss claim from making up the difference, and the hierarchy would fall through to step 6 `smoothing` on the amodimethicone — v0.2's value. `shine` is recorded as the conservative call because it is the value that does NOT depend on crediting a species the unresolved marker cannot place; `smoothing` is the value that does. Neither is auto-selected and both are on the record.

`shine` as a secondary is not at issue; `smoothing` is refused as a secondary because it would reuse the identical amodimethicone film that carries the primary — the double-count §6 rule 2 and D2 forbid.
`general` does not apply: a candidate cleared at step 5.
There is NO lamination property and no `lamination` focus value (charter F4, D2, evidence §7). Gloss identity is carried entirely by `shine`.
counterSignals: This is the most marker-sensitive focus call in the cohort, and all three of its recorded readings have now differed: v0.1 `shine` on a colourant marker, v0.2 `smoothing` on the recomputed allergen marker, v0.3 `shine` on the conservative unresolved read. The value should not be treated as settled until the marker is — which needs a verbatim exact-pack INCI, not another rule.

The conservative value is also the claim-flattering one here, which is uncomfortable and is stated rather than hidden. It is not the claim that produced it: criterion 3 was reached only after criteria 1 and 2 were established on the formula, and §9.5.1 forbids positioning from lowering a route's own threshold. Had criterion 1 genuinely failed, `shine` would fail with it regardless of how unambiguous the gloss claim is — which is exactly what v0.2 recorded.

`gloss_lamination_claim` fires, as it must for any Gloss/Glaze/Laminierung positioning: a human verifies that the shine threshold was tested independently and that the banned wording is absent. `tail_marker_unresolved` fires alongside it and names this field.
limitations: Banned wording, absolute (evidence §7, §9.5.4, R6a): this record never says seals, versiegelt, closes the cuticle, laminates, lasting, permanent, or builds a protective layer that stays — notwithstanding that the product's own pack uses two of those words. Permitted and used: temporary optical/surface emphasis, comparative surface-control potential.
Glycolic acid temporarily plasticises the fibre (a measured decrease in Young's modulus) and does not seal, bond, or produce lasting change; its skin-exfoliation evidence is not imported.

PROPYLENE GLYCOL (5) — one humectant, blocking `moisture` as a secondary

`moisture` is refused as a secondary at §9.5.3 criterion 1: PROPYLENE GLYCOL @5 is one humectant against a required three.

Re-checked under v0.3 (E2): unchanged. Neither marker reading creates a second endpoint — on the resolved reading the coconut oil would move the PRIMARY to smoothing rather than open a secondary slot.

focusCareVerdict.note: Re-derived under v0.3 (E2). The chosen focus is an optical one, so §9.5.1's repair/moisture verdict set does not apply and the verdict stays `not_applicable`; on the repair/moisture axis the formula would read `nonspecific` (no protein at any rank, one humectant, generic conditioning). `claim_role` REVERTS to `corroborating` with the focus: it points specifically at §9.5.4 criterion 3, the one claim-gated leg in this record, and the claim corroborated an optical architecture criteria 1 and 2 had already established from the formula alone. Under v0.2 this read `not_applicable`, because criterion 1 had failed and there was no route left to corroborate. `gloss_lamination_claim` fires as a review trigger under every reading.

blindToFinalChanges.reason: RESTORED under v0.3 (E2), having been withdrawn under v0.2. Blind, the formula clears §9.5.4 criteria 1 and 2 — an alignment-oriented amino silicone at rank 6, and no R4b heavy lipid established above the tail once §3.1.1 clause 2 withholds the coconut oil's credit — but criterion 3 requires exact-product Gloss/Glaze/Laminierung/Glanz positioning, which is by construction unavailable in a blind packet. The hierarchy therefore falls through to step 6 and returns `smoothing`. On unblinding, criterion 3 is satisfied unambiguously by the product name and claims, and `shine` is selected at step 5. This remains the only value change produced by unblinding anywhere in the cohort, and it is §11 step 4's first permitted channel working as designed — it is the reason the shine focus is claim-gated at all. Note the dependency chain: this change exists under v0.1 and v0.3 and not under v0.2, because it is live only while criterion 1 holds on the formula.
Consequential change following the primaryFocus change, via D2's deterministic benefits derivation.

No dual_supported tie, no bond claim, no lightness positioning to trigger the §9.2 conflict fallback, and no colour-protection positioning. In particular the gloss claim did NOT touch conditioning_level, care_direction, repair_support_level, the moisture guard, or the tail-marker plausibility assessment — §11 step 4 forbids all of them, and E2's limb is an ordinal test on the list, not a claim test.

adjudicationPoints.title: CLOSED by evidence (2026-10-06) — the ordering is real, the marker stays unresolved by house convention, the conservative values are FINAL
adjudicationPoints.body: The re-fetch E2 asked for is done: verbatim L'Oréal declaration (F.I.L. Z70038579/2, via rossmann.de product page, direct accordion extraction, 2026-10-06, GTIN/article 3600524128500) confirms the stored capture's ordering — HYDROXYCITRONELLAL @12, LIMONENE @18, LINALOOL @19, HEXYL CINNAMAL @28, GLYCOLIC ACID @29 and PARFUM LAST @30, CI colourants already @7–8. So the allergen-above-Parfum ordering is not a retailer transcription artifact: Parfum sits last by L'Oréal house convention and is not a concentration position at all. Per E2's own terms (ordering confirmed → marker stays unresolved → conservative values stand), the conservative reading is FINAL: weight_potential `moderate` (COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @9 sits in the unreadable zone — the colourant positions suggest the sub-1 % zone starts near @7), primary_focus `shine`, conditioning_level `moderate`, all capped by rule. The alternative rich/smoothing cascade is dead. The two secondary items (lexicon family-3 Cocos naming; §9.5.4 criterion-1 rank reading) remain standard-maintenance items for the freeze gate. For the record, the two conjuncts that can be checked would hold (no occlusive silicone stack — AMODIMETHICONE @6 is a single species; a single cationic surfactant in the credited head). This is a case where E4's new reachability is blocked by E2, and both rulings are working as intended.

fired.value: unresolved — HYDROXYCITRONELLAL @12 (declared fragrance allergen) with PARFUM/FRAGRANCE @30 (§3.1.1 third limb, E2)
fired.note: The marker-eligible species the R8 recomputation lands on cannot be believed: a declared allergen is a constituent of the fragrance compound and cannot outrank it by eighteen places in a descending-weight list. The marker is `unresolved`, it may neither qualify nor disqualify, confidence on every affected field is capped at `moderate`, and `tail_marker_unresolved` routes the record to review. Affected fields: weight_potential, primary_focus, conditioning_level, and the hair_thickness_fit echo — each carries both readings. R8's colourant demotion is unaffected and this record does not revert to the colourant at rank 7. The single action that would resolve this is a verbatim exact-pack INCI capture; the current source is retailer-aggregated.

v0AdjudicationPointStatus.AP-11-COLOURANT: CLOSED by R8, and NOT reopened by E2. A colourant may still not define the marker, and this record does not revert to CI 17200 @7. What E2 adds is a second test on the species R8's recomputation lands on: HYDROXYCITRONELLAL @12 is ordinally inconsistent with its own PARFUM @30, so the recomputed marker is `unresolved` rather than accepted. Precedence rule and plausibility rule are separate and neither is a fallback for the other.
